utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Summary of the witness, thank you very much. Summary of the witness statement. The witness was a member of Canary Island Tactical Task Force Spabat Canarias or Spanish Battalion, UNPROFOR, in Mostar area as from April through October 9, 1993. The Spanish Battalion UNPROFOR, Canarias arrived in the area of responsibility in April as hostilities broke out between Croats and Muslims. From the very beginning, the HVO command was against permanently deploying the SpaBat company in Mostar. It was deployed in Mostar on the 12th, 1993, after an armed conflict between HVO and ABiH had broken out on the 9th of May 1993. The main and primary mission of the SpaBat was to provide escorts for UNHCR, ICRC, and other officially recognised humanitarian organisations. They mainly protected and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can counsel please slow down? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: -- UNHCR and the ICRC in their activities. Although SpaBat was not officially in charge of the change of prisoners, they provided some support to the ICRC operations when visiting prisoners or refugees camps. Then later the mission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Poryvaev, you are still a bit too fast. It is difficult for the interpreters to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm happy to hear that I'm very fast in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. SpaBat and other international organisations had serious problems while fulfilling their functions because of the limited access to East Mostar, Caplina, Stolac and other areas. UNPROFOR members and humanitarian convoys were on many occasions targeted by HVO snipers and other troops.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the text and Mr. Poryvaev is reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: On the 11th of May, Spanish Battalion UNPROFOR Lieutenant Munoz Castellanos was killed by a grenade shot in a United Nations convoy delivering blood plasma and medicines to the Muslim war hospital in East Mostar. On the 11th of June, 1993, Spanish Battalion, UNPROFOR Lieutenant Jesus Aguilar Fernandez was killed by sniper in the area of the Hit building. The witness participated in the investigation of these facts. On the 9th and 10th of May 1993, Spanish Battalion UNPROFOR officers witnessed and filmed movement of about 400 Muslim civilians from Mostar towards the Heliodrom. This information was provided to the UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak. Witness visited Heliodrom together with General Morillon in Prado after the top meeting between Franjo Tudjman, Mate Boban, and Alija Izetbegovic in Medjugorje on the 18th of May 1993. The humanitarian situation in East Mostar, which was in fact isolated from other areas of Herceg-Bosna was extremely hard. The population did not have essential amount of food, water and medical assistance. For a long period of time, humanitarian convoys were pretended [sic] by HVO from delivering to East Mostar humanitarian aid. East Mostar was permanently shelled by HVO. Witness organised and participated in a number of meetings at high level between HVO and ABiH commanders. The witness saw General Slobodan Praljak on two occasions. In the witness's view, Slobodan Praljak symbolised courageous support to HVO. Witness met with HVO Defence Minister Bruno Stojic on a dozen of occasions. On the 17th of June, Witness negotiated with Bruno Stojic, the release of four Muslim United Nations interpreters who had been taken hostage. Later on, 17th of July, 1993, he had an unformal meeting with Bruno Stojic where the latter said that they, HVO, were able to solve the situation and that the loss of territory in certain areas was part of preconceived plan. The plan basically consisted of putting maximum pressure from the south of the town of Mostar. He also expressed his concern for the Muslim civilians living under the control of BiH army in East Mostar. He suggested and offered organising the evacuation of the largest possible number of those civilians. According to Stojic's calculations, the end of the story with two factions in Mostar, was a matter of 20 days to be solved. Witness also had contacts with other military commanders through HVO. Berislav Pusic was the head of HVO office for the exchange of displaced persons, prisoners, and bodies. His office was based in Mostar. SpaBat records have him registered as a civilian because he usually worked in plain clothes although he sometimes appeared in uniform. He was a the first SpaBat contact when there were requests for an exchange of prisoners. SpaBat received a lot of information about the expulsion of the Muslim population from various parts of Herceg-Bosna and transferring them to Muslim-populated areas or some third countries. SpaBat also received information about the conditions and numbers of detainees and the detention centres through numerous international organisations, non-government organisations, and passed it on to both HVO and ABiH and also to other relevant international agencies. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like with the assistance of the usher [Spanish translation coming over English channel] Your Honour, you have three binders and two separate -- one bundle of documents. I will explain why a little bit later. I think that we should not place the witness statements on the ELMO because we have a protected witness. He will work with hard copies, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, my question is, is it correct that you were interviewed by OTP investigators twice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: The first time you were interviewed on the 27th, 28th of November and 2nd, 3rd and 4th and 5th of December 1997, and this is Exhibit P10270.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: The second interview was conducted on the 2nd, 3rd, and 6th of July 2007, and this is our Exhibit P10217.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Just -- I would like witness to take first Exhibit 1027870, and this is a statement given in 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: It's binder 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Both in number -- yes. That's in error on the transcript. It's line -- page 18, line 1, actually, Exhibit number is 10270.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, take a look at this statement, first of all. My question is at the time you provided your witness statement, did you answer the questions of the investigator truthfully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you answer the questions freely, without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And now on -- I would like to you take a look at the last page of the statement. Do you see the last page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean page 11?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Is that your signature on your statement above the date, 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my signature, but the date was the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry, that's my error. Now I would like to take Exhibit 10217 and the same questions. Were your answers to the investigator truthful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, always.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you answer questions freely, without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I answered freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And I address you now to page 27, it's last page. Was this witness statement signed by yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you sign both these statements, you believe that they were just recorded to be true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They reflect what I experienced, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity of going through the statements when you had a meeting with myself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, we have already informed the Defence and the Trial Chamber that you made just some corrections in both statements. If you go now to our Exhibit 102717, this is statement given in July 2007, in paragraph 97, the last phrase, sentence, should be read as follows: "Two days after his death and with authorisation from the Croats, Vice Minister Bozic and my Colonel Morales, I went to the Bulevar area on the front line with my Lieutenant Hidalgo as an escort," and "two HVO military men" should be read instead of "Croatian military men," that was your correction, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, affirmative. I used the word "Croatian" wrongly. It should have been HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And now I will address to you page 22 of the same statement. This is paragraph 171. Is it correct -- have you found it? Is it correct that today, that today, during the meeting with myself, you noticed one mistake and this is, let's say, third line, "In that moment it was -- it was with the HV," should be removed because it's repeated twice. It has nothing to do with the check-points. It has something to do with Mr. Praljak, but it's clear from further continuation of the statement. Is it correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct. That was an unnecessary redundancy in the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And now let's go back to your statement given in December 1997. On page 5 of the statement, you also noticed two mistakes today, and I want to inform about it the Chamber and the Defence. "The Grey Wolves" -- have you found it, page 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have just found the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: The third passage from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: "The Grey Wolves, we have here were a Croatian snipers group." You explained that it should be "HVO group," and further and the last sentence says -- the last sentence, again, instead of "The two Croatian military men," you should have "HVO military men." Is it correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you have any other corrections to be made now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Poryvaev?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I wonder whether, in the first line of this paragraph, the last word, "Croatian military men" should not also be changed to "HVO."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just told that. Your Honours, I would like this exhibits -- these exhibits to be taken into evidence, I mean exhibit, I repeat the numbers, P10217, P10270.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has noted your request. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we should redact this? Witness, I want you to be very careful about your positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly order the redaction of line 1 to 3, and page 19: 19, 20, 21, 22. Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel. The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. I'm a little late in getting to my feet, but I think it would be a good idea to correct the transcript straight away. On page 20, lines 11 to 18, with reference to paragraph 171 of Exhibit 10217, I think that what my learned friend asked the witness or that is what was recorded on the transcript, that where the HV is mentioned first, which is the third line, that that be omitted because it's superfluous mentioning it twice because it's mentioned again with the description of General Praljak. Now, that's not true because according to the transcript, in the first sentence, which ends in line 3, it would appear just at that moment it was HVO, so the situation and the discussion was with the HVO, which means that the check-point was also HVO and not the HV as was erroneously stated, and the witness put that right but that should remain. So not the HV but the HVO. And then in the next sentence, the witness says, [In English] "From the Croatian army," [Interpretation] "General Praljak from the Croatian army," and then in brackets, "HV appeared at that moment." So that should stay because that's his statement. Whereas the Prosecutor said that the first HV should be -- was omitted and not that the HV was turned into the HVO. So it should have been HVO in view of all the other documents because the check-point was indeed a HVO check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the witness would explain. That's I just exposed his proposal as I was told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] (redacted), could you tell us how we should read paragraph 171, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour. I commented on the fact that it seemed that by saying it at that particular time General Praljak from the Croatian army and, in parentheses, "HV," reflected what was for me the position of General Praljak but it was redundant and wasn't needed. But the check-point was controlled by the HVO, not by the HV, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So as far as you're concerned General Praljak was part of the HVO and the check-point was an HVO check-point; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the check-point was HVO, and I never saw it as anything else and when I'm talking about this, I'm talking about the 11th of May, with a general who I understood to be HV at that particular time and I've mentioned that several times throughout my written statement because I understood that he was a general and I had met him two weeks prior, from the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it's more complicated than it seems to be at first sight. In the English version, it is stated and it gives the impression from what you say that General Praljak is an HV general, HV. This is something you maintain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Affirmative at that time General Praljak when I first met him was a general of the HV, Croatian army, and that's what came out in the press at the time. Later if that was changed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I would like just the Judges and the witness take just separate bundle without just carton binder, and it contains two exhibits, P10269 and P02108.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Just very shortly, what is the difference between these two documents? What is document 10269 stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document 269 is a copy, a literal copy, of my sworn statement from officials of the Spanish army. This is completed at the end of every year. It reflects what the army has in its records concerning my activity from my first day in the mission until the day I left the mission. Obviously, the Spanish army didn't think it was appropriate to provide the Court with documents concerning my activities prior to the period in question. It summarises the most important elements listed in my personal diary concerning my observations, comments and this was going to assist me in drafting in January of the following year my annual report. This was -- this was based on my personal observations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, could I conditionally, let's say, call it your personal diary, for practical purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative. It is my personal diary, but we have to bear in mind that as of the early the following year I had lost control over the copy that was made. This is the copy that the Spanish army made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And then let's go back to Exhibit P02108.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is a document drafted in Spanish by our task force and by my section. It reflects a summary on a daily basis of the summary -- the summary of the main events that occurred during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could I just call it again conditionally official diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative. I think, yes, it would be good to call it a logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Logbook. Then logbook. Your Honour I'm doing that for just practical purposes because we'll go back to these exhibits on many occasions, and I don't think that it's appropriate to call each time the number of exhibit. It will take just a while. Just for the -- if you agree with me, then for the record, for the records, Exhibit P02108, logbook. Exhibit P10269, personal diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Just one minor remark. This Exhibit 10269 of 11th of May, in which you mentioned General Praljak, in Spanish, [Spanish spoken] This is not to be found in the Exhibit 2108 because there is no mention at all of the 11th of May. So is there a reason for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the logbook, there were many people whose names were listed. They had attended meetings but not everybody's name was listed. I reflected that he was the [Spanish spoken] because that's what I had read in the press, and from the beginning our task force considered him as the [Spanish spoken].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, let's begin with one item which is called, let's say, deployment or -- of the SpaBat company in Mostar. Please take your statement for 2007 and go on back to paragraph 32. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I found paragraph 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: In this paragraph, you stated that there were two rounds of meetings with HVO leadership and in particular with Slobodan Bozic about the deployment of your company on a permanent basis in Mostar, and you also stated here that HVO was against the decision of deploying company. My first question: Why did you want your company to be deployed in Mostar on a permanent basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a practical problem. Our mission in supporting the UNHCR missions would have benefited if we had had deployment in Mostar, which is halfway between [indiscernible] and Jablanica. And it would have avoided a lot of unnecessary vehicular movement along the road. That was the main reason for -- that was the main reason prior to the conflict. As to your second question, why did the HVO oppose this, we wanted -- I think they found excuses such as we wanted to be in areas controlled by them, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to take just your logbook, and this is an entry of the 26th of April 1993, in both binders, in all versions, page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What date, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: 26th of -- I'm sorry, 26th, 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my personal diary, I don't have the 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I'm talking about logbook.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I made a mistake. 26th of April, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. On page 2, for the 4th of May, you also have some entry about discussion with Mr. Slobodan Bozic about deployment of company. Witness, do these two entries reflect what really happened and which is described in paragraph 32 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative. We were putting a lot of pressure on because we needed to be situated, we needed to use some headquarters or some facilities to base our operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: In paragraph 44, 45, 46 of the same statement dated 2007 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: You claim that the company was deployed finally after the 20th -- 12th of May 1993, after the interference of the international community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Let's go back to your logbook and to the entry for the 12th of May 1993, page 5 in English, page 4 in Spanish, and I suggest page 5 also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Does it correspond that this meeting really took place, and the people from international organisations were involved in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Next, I would just turn you to Exhibit P02366. This is binder 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Petkovic wanted to say something. Yes, please, General. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just need to intervene in view of a technical matter. It wasn't deployment in Mostar due to pressure by the international community but no, it was due to the signatures of General Morillon and Mr. Thebault. That is why UNPROFOR was deployed in Mostar between the 12th and the 13th. It was not due to pressure exerted by the international community. That's it. There was a document that says that. So I just -- well, does the witness know that or does he not know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] (redacted), I suppose you've heard what General Petkovic has just said. What do you think of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the information that I have, there was obviously a lot of pressure on all levels, and it's true that there was this meeting with Ambassador Thebault at the end of which SpaBat got permission to set up base in Mostar. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I turn you to Exhibit P02366, binder 2. That's item Mostar, page 4, 5 English, page 2 Spanish, page 4 B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before continuing, could I please ask for an extra table to -- or a chair, perhaps, to hold some of these documents? Yes. 2366.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Page 2 in Spanish, 4/5 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: The witness, do you recognise this document you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Just leaf down the information you have, leaf through the information you have. Does it correspond that you just explained the Trial Chamber about the circumstances in which the company was deployed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, affirmative. This reflects a time period in which the transfer was completed. In other words, we were originally in -- on both sides of the confrontation line and later we were able to be deployed halfway between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I think that I will finish with this topic for the moment and pass on to another one, if you allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I will skip now just relevant to Heliodrom because I think we dwelt quite much on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: But only question, one only question, Witness, is it correct that there were three visits to Heliodrom in May by representatives of international organisations, not one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And you participated in one of these, just, visits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative. I took part in what I think is the third of the three visits that I know of, which was on the 20th with a general, Prado.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And in paragraph 130, you claim that detention camps were not just issues of your responsibility, they were the matter which is for intelligence service and so on and so forth. I mean your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the -- this is true for the mission that I took part in. It was an inspection of the facilities. In this case, I went taking advantage of General Prado's visit to -- getting information, that is true, that was not my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And let's go now to Exhibit P -- okay, that's let's say personal diary, personal diary, entry for the 11th of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. On page 6 of the Spanish version, 11th of June. What would you like me to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. "I attended a meeting with HVO officials, who were informed of the concern of the international community regarding the imprisonment of a large number of Muslims from West Mostar at the Croatian-held Heliodrom to the south of the town." Is this entry correct? Does it reflect the situation that there were detainees in Heliodrom in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, my next topic will be just freedom of movement of the population within the Mostar town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if it takes you five minutes, we can do it now. If it takes more time, we would rather -- we had better have the break now. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will take a little bit more. More than five minutes. Then maybe after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Let's break now. 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. You have the floor, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: So we are talking about the freedom of movement for the population of Mostar. Witness, I would like you to take a look at paragraph 79 of your last witness statement. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: This paragraph deals with problems with the movement of the population from West Mostar to East Mostar and vice versa and it's stated here that Muslims, the people, Muslims were allowed to leave freely West Mostar for East Mostar, but were not allowed on many occasions to move from East Mostar to West Mostar and therefore SpaBat raised a protest in view of the situation and they explained also that you elevated these problems to Joko [phoen] Mountain, Kiseljak, and tried to solve the problem at this level. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to you take binder 2 and take a look at Exhibit P02583.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: This is INTREP 188 dated the 31st of May. It's English page 8, Spanish page 3, and B/C/S page 6, I think. Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Is it authentic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It reflects around the 31st of May, in the morning, the information that we handed to the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. In this document you also stated that Croatian authorities were contacted by SpaBat. Bozo Raguz said that the joint commission and its decisions were history, and consequently all travel from one side of the river to the other was cancelled, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. In fact, it's mentioned that that's the person included.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I address you to paragraph 8 -- 81 of your statement, and it was established -- you say here -- that the passage of civilians from one bank of the Neretva River to the other by bus was hindered by HVO. The HVO had been picking the Muslim persons who should cross, and again you say here about the letter of protest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What I would like to clear up now, what do you mean or did you mean by saying that they were picking the Muslim persons who were allowed to cross or not to cross? What was the criteria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two situations. Certain age groups were not allowed to move if they were Muslim to the west -- from the west to the east. These were in particular men of fighting age. That was the first criteria, and this goes against the terms of the agreement that was reached. And then we had the elderly, children, these people were not allowed to cross back by the HVO. So SpaBat wrote a letter protesting to the authorities about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to take a look at Exhibit P02507 [sic], it's also binder 2. And page 3/4 English, page 3/4 in English, page 1 in Spain. This is SITREP now 188, 31st of May 1993. Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Does it reflect the situation with the Muslim population you just explained to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know whether you said it this way. In the record it says 2507, but I think you are actually using 2570.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, yes, Your Honour, I'm sure it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm looking at 2570.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Then in paragraph 86 you stated, "The situation was so serious that UNPROFOR Kiseljak sent to Zagreb the following report in which they raised this issue very seriously before the superior UNPROFOR." And now I ask you to take a look at Exhibit P02582, binder 2, as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document goes from Kiseljak to Zagreb with the Spanish Battalion in copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And here they say, "Complaint to HVO headquarters was sent by SpaBat, HVO is not entitled to do any selections because of the cease-fire agreement established free pass to all personnel," is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct, and it reflects the actions that SpaBat was taking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: So Your Honour, I accomplished one of my additional questions that was not sufficiently clear to the Prosecution. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like to move further to situation with the freedom of movement for humanitarian and UNPROFOR convoys. In paragraph 91 of the statement you claim on the 30th of May 1993, section received information from section 2 that three Irish drivers working for humanitarian organisations had been arrested by HVO police. You dealt with HVO authorities for more than six hours and finally achieved to release them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, were you also involved in this situation personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to check my diary. I think we were calling, but I would like to check that in my diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Just take -- I would like you to take a look at your personal diary, and that should be entry for the 30th of May as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Affirmative. In my diary, I say that I was taking part in this -- in these negotiations with them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to turn you to Exhibit 02583, binder 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The same that we are dealing with right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. This -- yes, INTREP, yes, 188, 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. And here among other information, page 8, 9 in English, Spanish page 3, B/C/S page 6, I suggest they describe the situation why the people, Irish people, drivers, were arrested, and what was just presented as a gift to them. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I found it. I don't understand the idea of the gift.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Well, yes. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I recognise the document. I don't know if there was a translation problem. I recognise the problem. It reflects everything that was done to try to get the three drivers released with the problems that we had had at the check-point and finally, yes, this was resolved thank you, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like you to take a look at Exhibit 03371. This is binder 1 now. Page 8 in English, Spanish page 2, second passage from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And is the situation described correctly in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative. It says that they -- all UNPROFOR vehicles heading to Mostar are stopped, permission will not be given to enter the city for one month. By the end of July this should be lifted. This was dated the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And next just miscellaneouses, if you go back to page 10 of English version and Spanish version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Item 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Are you dealing with the situation described here when one convoy was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was quite a regular problem with check-points. Our convoys were often held up. This is no -- by no means an exceptional case. It's just one of that many occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Then, witness, do you authenticate this SpaBat INTREP 228 dated on the 10th of July, I mean this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I authenticated this document, 288. Signed on the 9th of July 1993. It does accurately reflect the information put forward on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Then I will address to you Exhibit 03311. This is binder 1 again. English --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: -- pages 7 and 8, from 7 to 8, Spanish page 4, bottom page -- bottom passage, B/C/S page 8. This item Mostar. And in this document, they also deal with the situation with humanitarian and mediation missions between the factions and every day Spanish patrols were being stopped at the check-point to the south of Mostar and held for several hours, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. This is a summary from the 14th of June to the 5th of July. It explains that attacks were frequent during those weeks while humanitarian missions were being conducted. Every day, patrols were detained at the check-points and then certain problems were outlined more concretely to do with the Muslim neighbourhoods. Thank you, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Then, witness in paragraph 95 on your statement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: You deal with the situation when after the incident involving an Irish lorry, the HVO ordered its snipers to open fire on all civilian or military vehicles except for UNPROFOR vehicles and so on and so forth. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct. It reflects what was brought forward to the authorities' attention on the 31st of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to take a look at Exhibit P02593. This is binder 2, topic, areas of information, English page 8, Spanish page 3, page 8, I think B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't found it. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. 02593. In Spanish this is page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: This is a SpaBat INTREP 189 for the 31st of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, 189, 189, of 31st of May, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. Witness, now let's go back to your personal diary. The entry for the 15th of June 1993, page 6, bottom passage, page 6 in the English, page 7 in Spanish. It may be -- if I'm not mistaken, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're not talking about the 15th of June, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 13th of June, yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Of course, witness, this information concerns personally you. Is it correct that you received some kind of threats from the commander of the team of Croatian snipers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just as it is written here in my diary, our military intelligence service were aware of the problem concerning these snipers, and the colonel relayed the information to me that way because I had taken part officially in the verifications to see whether our Lieutenant had been killed by such fire. For a few days I was not allowed to leave our barracks. That is totally correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we'll go further to our next topic, which concerns Mr. Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps before we go on, one reads in the transcript that -- I quote more or less page 37, line 4, that the HVO after the incident with the Irish lorries ordered the snipers to shoot at SpaBat representatives. How do you know this? Have you seen such an order or what explains this statement? What is it based upon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It does not say that they fired against us but that they fired against any vehicle, including us. In theory, we never thought that this was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Except for UNPROFOR vehicles, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And you just assumed that there has been such an order because you observed the shooting, or did you have some sort of inside information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information giving open slather to the snipers to open fire on vehicles came via the military intelligence service, and this is reflected in the INTREP that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: May I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, let's go to paragraph 113 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Here you mention that you just had seen Mr. Bruno Stojic some 10 or 12 times, and on the 17th of June you had contact with Mr. Stojic during six hours of negotiations in which I had to pressure him to free four Muslim interpreters working with UNH military observers. Could you explain why did it take too long to solve this problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct. I can explain this, and this is reflected in the exhibits. Essentially the problem was that they were four interpreters that had been detained by HVO elements in the Konjic pocket in the isolated remote northern part. It would appear that they had -- that there was no power over them. There were many attempts, vis-a-vis General -- I think the General Keza Zarko was one of the people involved in the letter to our minister so he could try to resolve the situation but it was a very delicate situation. We were not aware of this issue until we were told about it, and finally, Minister Stojic gave us, was given -- satellite communications means which meant that he could relay the order to the relevant authorities to order their release, so this took a lot of time and that's how the release was finally obtained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did he act just with desire to solve this problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am convinced that, yes, that he had all the goodwill necessary to get the problem resolved. But it was not easy for him to get this order across because there was a different calendar of events that Colonel Ganic had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to you take a look at SITREP 205, Exhibit P02794. This is binder 3. Binder 3, page 5/6 English, page 3 Spanish, B/C/S 4/5, topic Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, naturally. It's a SITREP 216. I can't read my copy very well, but I think it's the 15th of June, the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Is the situation reflected correctly in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. Our officials there informed us that on that day, the date of the document, there were representatives of organisations who had gone into that enclave, they had only gone with interpreters and not with UNPROFOR protection, and they went there and so the beginning of the problem was outlined there. At that time, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: That's enough. That's enough. Now let's move to next exhibit, this is 205 SITREP -- yes, 205 bis. 17th of June 1993, exhibit P02804, binder 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Is the situation reflected correctly in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you authenticate this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And finally, now let's move to Exhibit P02808, binder 3, SITREP 206, dated 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. I have it here before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Is the development of events reflected in the document correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this reflects what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I would like to go to some other topic relevant to Mr. Stojic and this is paragraph 122 of the statement. But, Your Honour, I would like maybe to move into private session because otherwise, we can reveal the names of people concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I invite you to take a look at paragraph 129 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And in this paragraph, you stated that I didn't know about any specific relations between Bruno Stojic and special units, but we had information from section 2 coming from SpaBat INTREP 270 and 70, that he had passed a special confidence in some HVO units as Ludvig Pavlovic, Bruno Stojic, and units under Tuta's command. Sorry, take a look at Exhibit P04401. And this is binder 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have the document in front of which I confirm is from the [indiscernible] from the 21st of August, and it states that according to the superior authorities and HVO that there are units in which they had a lot of trust and these were Bruno Stojic, Ludvig Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Our next topic is relevant to Mr. Slobodan Praljak. In paragraph 167 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: You say that in your previous statements and your current statement, you stated that you considered Mr. Slobodan Praljak as HVO military who represented the interests of President Tudjman in Herceg-Bosna, and I said it with respect to my first meeting with him on the 29th of April when he was dressed in HVO -- HV, sorry, military uniform. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The first time I met this person whom I later learned was General Praljak, he was dressed in the Croat uniform and according to the local press, and because photos had been taken of him, he was at that time an important person in the Croat chiefs of staffs. Then I had occasion to meet him twice later and I managed to speak to him via interpreters, but my first encounter with him was when he was dressed in HV fatigues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now, let's move to Exhibit 02 -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Witness, you said that he wore the HV uniform. Now, how do you make the difference between the HVO uniform and the HV uniform or whether it's the US army uniform or the Russian army uniform? On what do you base yourself to make the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before a mission the Spanish army trains its people, its personnel. Over seven weeks we were under training and we were taught how to identify the different uniforms. First of all, obviously, furthermore, he was not dressed in combat uniform. He was not in fact dressed in fatigues. He was dressed in the uniform, in the street uniform, if you will have, and he was furthermore identified by the press. By no means was it reason for surprise to find him there. He was in fact known as the person President Tudjman trusted in the area. That was the situation at the time, and of course at the time we knew who was who in the different uniforms. However, however, president -- and I agree with you, the uniformity in combat was indeed great, and there were people dressed with uniforms with flags that had nothing to do with anything, or people dressed in mixed uniforms. However, when it comes to General Praljak, the first time I saw him in Medjugorje, he was dressed in the Croat uniform, in what we would call the presentation uniform. He was easily identifiable, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now, witness I invite to you take a look at Exhibit P02419. This is binder 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Could you identify this document? What this document is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a version in Spanish. It's my statement on the 16th of May about the event that took place on the 11th of May. It's a document I drafted in the area before Spanish military Judge accompanied by a court usher, and in Spanish, there is questioning within the official procedures following the death in combat of Lieutenant Munoz Castellanos. Basically to sum up, I am asked about the mission as to why I was in Mostar. I explained that in the 11th of May we had been ordered to take plasma and drugs to the Armija hospital in Mostar, and we had an authorisation from the minister, from Stojic, a written permit, a written authorisation, in order to enter the city, and in this written document, agreed upon by two factions we would be able to visit the HVO prisoners detained by the Armija, and we would in fact, return to Croats -- to the Croat area a catholic priest whose name I give. For reasons that escape me we were only allowed to enter with the two APCs, and therefore we were very few, apart from the doctor whose name is here, from the International Red Cross, who was responsible for the mission. So this is an International Red Cross mission which is being served by UNPROFOR and of which I was responsible. I'm accompanied by a third commander who is interested in learning what the situation is like in Mostar, from the operational side. As a single escort we had Lieutenant Munoz Castellanos. The others were in fact crew of the armoured personnel carrier. The judge requests me, where were you? What happened? And basically the aim was to take plasma to the hospital as agreed upon. Second, we were to visit the prisoners. I personally got a list of the names of the prisoners that would later be given over to UNHCR and the Red Cross via the official channel so as to assert that these people are alive. We give over these lists, and when we are about to pick up the Catholic priest, we were accompanied by a general, a brigadier general of the Armija, General Humo -- there were two brothers, but the other one apparently died a few days later. At that time, we were travelling towards the area where this priest was detained so that he could be handed over. The armoured personnel carrier cannot come with us because we are talking about very narrow streets and lanes, as you are well aware in Muslim Mostar. And at some stage, a number of shots are heard, two in fact, mortar shots are heard. Some rests or the impact was very close. There was tremendous smoke. We picked up the priest. We told him to pick up his belongings as soon as possible. We run with him and as we are returning to our armoured personnel carriers, I noticed a group of people around a soldier whom I thought at the time was an Armija soldier who perhaps had fainted, and we were then informed that it is one of our lot and referring to our Lieutenant who was lagging somewhat behind from us. We realised then and then that he had been wounded, terribly wounded, because the shrapnel in fact -- he's riddled with shrapnel. We picked him up and take him to the very hospital where we had delivered the plasma before. At that time, the very Armija doctors explained to us that the person was seriously wounded and had to be evacuated to hospital. The Lieutenant at that time could speak. We were all -- couldn't speak, rather. We were all tremendously afraid. It was the first time that such an incident in which one of ours had been wounded so seriously. It was then that the commander coming with me stayed back with interpreter so the interpreter could in fact do her job, and I together with a driver and one armoured personnel vehicle, I leave the city in order to try and see whether we could get the ambulance that we had come with through but had been detained at the check-point. So when I -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry -- back where were you detained -- deployed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were detained by the HVO that controlled that access to the city of Mostar from Medjugorje. I had no interpreter by then, but the Lieutenant's section interpreter was there. I in fact get them aboard the ambulance together with medical, Spanish medical officer, and I tried to access the city to pick up the lieutenant, the wounded lieutenant. Tremendous tension erupted at the first check-point. I said quite unequivocally that either they let me through, or I would run them over. I was allowed through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Slower a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm getting carried away because I'm in fact recalling what the situation was like. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: On what occasion did you see Mr. Praljak? Let's go straight to the point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were arriving at that point where there was a first check-point. We were in fact stopped but finally we just got through by just putting the vehicle in front, and there was a second check-point some 100 metres down. Some 20 militiamen with anti-tank or anti-personnel carrier weaponry waited for us. I don't understand what was going on, so I said please could I have the person in charge here?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Please, slow, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise to the courtroom once again. So I request that some representative of the authority come. I even showed the authorisation from Minister Stojic, but nobody paid heed to my words. Remember that we have two vehicles. We have an ambulance clearly marked as such, and it was then that General Slobodan Praljak, whom I met three weeks before, comes. I explain through the interpreter what the situation is, and he solved the problem saying, "Let them through." And we went through, we went through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, just one question. In your statement, you just firmly stressed that his presence -- I mean General Praljak -- demonstrated the direct involvement of the Croat republic in the conflict. Why did you draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, remember, this report I drafted in Medjugorje four or five days after the death of our Lieutenant in action, and I attach photos of General Praljak that had appeared in the local press. I also informed my own military authorities, I also let them know what my personal opinion was; to wit, that if three weeks ago he was in HV uniform and today he is the authority that allows a check-point to let us through, he is obviously very easily identifiable. But it was up to that point my own personal opinion. During those days there were very many interrogation marks in the world of military intelligence as to what type of support there may be from the HV for HVO. To me, those dilemmas were dispelled in my mind the moment I realised that it was General Praljak who solved the problem. And I'll always be thankful to him that he solved this problem; on his personal authority the militiamen allowed me to go through with the ambulance. I stated this before the Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now I would like the witness to move to Exhibit P02464. This is binder 2. Witness, could you identify this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is my own statement signed on the 20th of May with the explanation of the narration of the events. It's an official document which requests -- which is request by UNPROFOR from all the people involved in an incident or event in which a member of UNPROFOR dies. I had to sign it because of the Red Cross convoy incident, and I explained who were part of the convoy and what events took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you confirm your just information about General Praljak given in this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's my statement, my signature, 20th of May, and I say quite clearly that General Praljak appeared and following a brief conversation with me, he officially gave orders for us to be let through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another question: Witness, did you ever have information of Mr. Praljak being in command of any military operation on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are referring to that particular moment? I have not quite understood your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. My question was: Did you ever have any information of Mr. Praljak, Slobodan Praljak, General Slobodan Praljak, being in command of any particular military operation on the territory of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. From that moment onward, General Praljak was the most visible person for SpaBat, and some important events such as the check-point convoy stoppage in which he showed the power, having his capacity, I don't know exactly what his mission was in all this. That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And do you remember him being in command of operation, I asked you, military operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, right now, I cannot recall. If you are referring to specific action I remember that in certain reports from our unit, from the Spanish unit, it was stated that on the orders of General Praljak, certain actions took place. To me, he was at a given point the military authority. I don't know what his exact relation or his position was in the minister General Petkovic structure or line of command. I don't know whether this is what you're getting at. Are you asking whether he was involved in some infantry attack? I mean obviously, I don't know. I don't know whether you're referring to an exhibit or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to you take a look at Exhibit P02902. Binder 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have it here in front of me, this document. INTREP 211, 22nd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What is it about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a daily summary, talking about the area of Mostar, where it describes actions taken and the Jablanica area. I understand that the Prosecution is referring to the fact that in the Konjic, Jablanica document, at point 1 it talks about Vosjovika [phoen] conflicts and HVO troops were under the command of General Praljak. Obviously this is a document stemming from the SpaBat, and if they wrote this down it's because they had information. But my personal relations with General Praljak did not enable me to identify his exact military role.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see that in this document, it's the second paragraph, they say that in the area HVO troops of Jusuf Prazina and Mladen Naletilic, known as Tuta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I see the second part, the second affirmation in this report, and the HVO troops of Jusuf, they entered -- Naletilic known as Tuta and point 3 according to BiH sources they were troops transported. There was a joint commission in which 25 soldiers were involved. Yes. I remember this report. This was a report sent by our second section. I confirm this document, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I covered one additional question that I wanted to ask this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now let's move to Mr. Berislav Pusic. In paragraph 88 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. This question concerns Mr. Pusic. I have a follow-up question to put to the witness. After the death of the Lieutenant, you told us that you made a statement. This is Exhibit number 2419. I listened very carefully to what you said. We also have the statement in Spanish, and it seems as if a Spanish judge took the declaration in the presence of a secretary because I believe there are three signatures on this document, your signature, the signature of the secretary, and the signature of the judge. Are you quite sure that we are talking about a judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when a Spanish company of more than 500 men, and in our case, around 2.000 men, is always accompanied by one legal adviser. This is a member of the military's legal service, which is there in order to offer legal advice support, and they offer -- they have national legal authority, because it is understood that it is often very difficult to bring a judge from Spain to open a case. In our case this was our legal adviser, I won't say the number -- I won't say the name but the name is listed in the documents. And the legal adviser was here in order -- maybe the legal adviser we have here in the courtroom will be able to give us more information on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that the statement which you made and gave to this legal adviser was to be part of an investigation that was conducted by a military prosecutor or investigating judge. I don't know who the person might have been.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That person is part of the Spanish company and is there to open a case if ever there is a fatal casualty among the Spanish [indiscernible]. He performs legal functions. He has all the weight of our legal structures, and he may undertake functions as a prosecution, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So an investigation was conducted. What were the findings of this investigation, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, of course, I didn't take part in the investigation; although, I was one person involved in the occurrence. I supported, as best I could, those who were conducting the investigation to identify photographs taken in Mostar, to offer assistance where I could. When the investigation concluded, I did take the time to read the entire file. It was the Lieutenant who escorted me, and one of the most difficult areas of our mission is to explain to the widow or to the surviving family members of the deceased how the person, their son, their husband, was killed. I had to do that. I had to honour my duty as a Spanish military staff member. I had to say how and where the death occurred. I don't know if you would like to provide me more information or whether that is -- would you like me to tell you where the fire came from or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will go to the heart of the matter straight away. According to the investigation, which seemingly was undertaken, who shot this Lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We always had some doubt initially because what is sure is that -- if it were mortar fire or a grenade, then it's very clear -- it's not clear where it would come from. Grenades and mortar fire leaves a trace. It enables you to identify the area from where it came. But if, even after a few days, even if there has been rain, there will be rust to tell you where the grenade came from. The grenade that we felt was the one that caused the impact has been identified, and the Spanish person conducting the investigation identified the angle of impact. We had no doubt that the impact was not from the Serbian area because initially we wondered if the Serbs were taking advantage of the confusion, but we ruled that out. It was not a Serbian attack. The cone of access corresponding to this grenade, in particular the grenade that killed lieutenant, was Mount Hum and this was under the control of the HVO troops. I don't know if you would like more information, but initially that's what I can say. That's where we determined it was from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Let's go back to Mr. Berislav Pusic. Did you know a person whose name is Berislav Pusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: In paragraph 88 and 89 of your statement, you just describe what his position was and functions. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was always identified to me as the person in charge of the office for the exchange of displaced persons, prisoners, and bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you ever see him -- did you ever see him --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, I had met with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like you to take a look at Exhibit 04870. This is binder 3. English page 4, Spanish page 5. The meeting concerning the exchange of prisoners. Have you found --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I'm getting there. You said 4870, page 5; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see under other information, item 3, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Meeting concerning the exchange of prisoners. This is the last passage in the whole of the document, last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it, I have it, I have it. Yes, it's under other information, page 5, information concerning the exchange of prisoners which was supposed to happen in Medjugorje, under SpaBat supervision and HVO and BiH. Yes, the BiH authorities affirmed that they would not deliver the prisoners until Mr. Pusic of the HVO had given his word by telephone, et cetera, is that right? Yes, I identify this as a paragraph of a report sent by SpaBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now let's move to your personal diary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Page 9, 8th August. Page 9 if I may suggest --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. Because firstly it was one of the first times that I was allowed out of the area, and I took part as a member of UNPROFOR in a meeting with Granic, and I -- and we had Mr. Pusic from HVO, and there were international humanitarian agencies present as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And in paragraph 90 of the statement, there is one allegation that I would like you to explain the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: "In my previous statement I mentioned on page 7 that Mr. Pusic was a sort of mafiosi." Where did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps -- perhaps it's not really my place to say this to this Trial Chamber, but what I was stating was that the comment that I heard from two interpreters, apart from all of the Bosnians, Muslims, Serbs, and Croats that I had under my command, they called him something along these lines, like a mafia member, and that's why in my head I had this image or this expression describing him, mafia man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we can move to our new topic if you will allow me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Before you move on to another topic, just one small point of clarification, witness. A while ago we saw a document in which it is mentioned that the exchange of prisoners was supervised in Spanish under -- was supervised by, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's not and never was a responsibility of UNPROFOR forces to take part in any prisoner exchange. This was a responsibility of the International Red Cross, as an international organisation, our job as UNPROFOR was to support the Red Cross, but not always could the International Red Cross Medjugorje and Mostar, not always could they be available. So with the two parties in conflict -- actually you had three groups in conflict, because at times you could include Serbia, theoretically although it never occurred, and so there was the expectation that the presence of UNPROFOR was going to make sure that everything was done fairly. As we, as UNPROFOR, never took part in the exchange of prisoners, this was an issue that perhaps might have used the services of one of our patrols to ensure the safety of the exchange in certain areas. We were there to support. As has been reflected, there was one and there is -- this is also reflected in the documents. Our -- the headquarters in Medjugorje commands or units sent from the Spanish Battalion were able to provide support personnel. Very often the agreements between the two sides were not actually respected, and our role was only to ensure the safety with the International Red Cross in theory being the international organisation to ensure prisoner exchange. Our role was to support the Red Cross. We were supposed to ensure that they didn't kill each other, but we never took part directly in prisoner exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While you were talking, I was reviewing the document which the Prosecutor showed you a while ago, number 4870. I was reading it in Spanish. I wasn't reading it in English. And in Spanish, one really has the feeling that the meeting on the exchange of prisoners, which was supposed to be held manana on the next day, in Medjugorje, you wrote here, that this was to be supervised by SpaBat, and supervision by SpaBat, this means something. That is what I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Under the supervision of the SpaBat is talking about the meeting, not the exchange. This is the meeting to do with the exchange. It's not actually the exchange itself. Why? Because our general headquarters were there to supervise and to ensure that no one killed anyone else, and it was about this meeting, not about the exchange. Perhaps it's not been drafted in a way that reflects that, but what I'm saying is to do with the meeting, and I can say that as a head of the union. So SpaBat was there because both groups wanted SpaBat to be there present so that there would be no cheating on the terms of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move to our -- my new topic, but maybe it makes sense to make a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that we have just about reached the two hour mark. Could you please check this? We shall now have a 20-minute break, and we shall resume in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution according to our calculation has ten minutes and not a minute more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Shall I start? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, now we should cover the very important issue but very fast. Forceful transferring of the population. I will address you to your logbook. 16th of May. Attention -- have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Protection of 54 Muslim refugees in [indiscernible] who were expelled by police after their lorries had been stolen. Do you confirm this entry in your logbook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I was waiting for the end of the translation, yes, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: 20 of June arrival of 104 refugees from Posusje. Do you confirm this entry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: 21st of June, contacts with Isabella, organisation to continue --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I also confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. And then 15th of August, this same document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Contact with UNHCR to discover problem of or expulsion 150 Muslims from the area of Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: 24th of August, here, information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: 800 Muslims, refugees, mainly women, children and elderly who had been taken by the HVO to the Vrci zone in buses and forced to come forward to Dreznica. Do you confirm this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Then same exhibit, 8th of September, SpaBat negotiated in the evacuation of 300 displaced persons who had been expelled from Croatian area of Radjan [phoen], is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And now I would like you to take a look at Exhibit P04505, binder 3. This is page 6 English, page 3 Spanish, INTREP 274, 25th of August, that's about 800 Muslims again to confirm this document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: -- information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, document -- office document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down, please and pause between question and answer? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Exhibit P03587, binder 3. Yes, page 9 English. This is SpaBat INTREP 238?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... "The UNHCR has informed of a plan drawn up by the HVO whereby it intend to send out 10.000 Muslims to Croatia. The idea was the Muslims to find temporary residence after receiving transit visas with the help of the Croatian authorities. They asked UNHCR for assistance. However, the UNHCR refused to participate in the operation which would have amounted to ethnic cleansing because it did not include the possibility of the return of people who were living [indiscernible] for their property. Do you confirm this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Since a lot of time has run away, maybe, Your Honour, I will conclude my examination-in-chief. Thank you very much for your attention and patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
